newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: GOLF-RAIN SUSPENDS FIRST ROUND PLAY.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-RAIN SUSPENDS FIRST ROUND PLAY.

text.p: Heavy overnight and morning rain forced suspension of play after just 1-1/2 hours in the first round of the Million Dollar Challenge at the Gary Player Country Club on Thursday.
Play was eventually suspended early in the afternoon after 22 millimetres of rain fell on the course during the morning.
Some of the greens had become unplayable, according to tournament referee Dennis Bruyns, while most of the saturated bunkers on the course were "unfair".
Bruyns said the 15-year-old tournament had never had an uncompleted day's play.
He said the first round would resume early on Friday morning with the second round beginning on time in the afternoon, weather permitting.
German Bernhard Langer, the winner in 1985 and 1991, set the early pace in the persistent drizzle with American Steve Stricker and four-times European number one Colin Montgomerie of Britain.
With the players able to take preferred lies on the fairways to clear mud from their balls, Langer and Stricker moved to two-under before dropping shots at the 440-yard fifth hole.
Montgomerie birdied the 553-yard second to share the lead when play was suspended.
Nick Price of Zimbabwe, Welshman Ian Woosnam, titleholder Corey Pavin, fellow-American Mark Brooks, the U.S. PGA champion, South African Ernie Els and American Mark O'Meara were all level par.
Completing the field are Masters champion Nick Faldo of Britain, British Open champion Tom Lehman and U.S. Open champion Steve Jones, both Americans.
Pavin said the decision to start play on time in the morning was fully justified.
"The big question mark was with the bunkers and the tournament committee decided to go out and play - and that was fine.
"Everybody had the same situation and everyone knew that you had to try and avoid the bunkers! If you hit it into casual water in the bunkers and had to drop, your ball could plug in the bunker.

"I didn't take my own advice very well because I drove in the bunker at the first hole and had to do that. It's unfortunate that the tournament couldn't stay on schedule but I think, by the end of tomorrow, we'll be right back on track."
